title: feat(spec,lint)!: refuse allowDelete: false beside modifyAllRecords: true
body:
Fixes #25575

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed
Ruling-ref: 6377890121 (letter A, under 6377842908); retriage 6382861731

## What changes

`modifyAllRecords` stays the write bypass for edit, delete and transfer (the runtime and `MODIFY_ALL_WRITE_KEYS` are untouched). What an author can write narrows:

- **Schema refusal.** `ObjectPermissionSchema` refuses an explicit `allowDelete: false` in an entry that sets `modifyAllRecords: true`: one `custom` issue at `objects.OBJECT.allowDelete` (wildcard `*` included). The message names the route for "edit every record, delete none". It rides the existing `checkScopeAgainstSuperUserBits` refinement (the #16870 precedent), so the response-side `EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema` stays tolerant.
- **Omitted key materialises as `true`.** A raw-input stage in front of the schema writes `allowDelete: true` into an entry that sets `modifyAllRecords: true` and omits `allowDelete`. See "Mechanism assumption" below for why the refinement alone could not work.
- **Lint arm.** `security-modify-all-delete-withheld` (error) in the security-posture family (`packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts`), with an `os explain` entry. On parsed doors the schema refuses first, so the arm reaches the unparsed doors only (`os lint` on a raw object-literal config, a direct call), the same posture `security-owd-alias` documents.
- **Data at rest.** ADR-0087 D2 conversion `permission-modify-all-allow-delete-false-to-true` (retired from the load path from day one, `retiredAfter: '18.1.0'`) plus the D3 entry `permission-modify-all-allow-delete-false-refused`. Stored rows and built artifacts inside their declared-floor window get the inert `false` rewritten to the `true` the evaluator always acted on. A source authored at the current surface is refused, not rewritten.
- **Docs.** A measured recipe in `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx` ("Recipe — edit every record, delete none"); one paragraph in `permissions-matrix.mdx`; two table rows in `permission-sets.mdx` / `permission-metadata.mdx` that said Modify All is "edit" now say "edit and delete". Generated references regenerated.

## Mechanism assumption (re-measured, and why the shape differs from "a parse-time refinement")

`allowDelete` carries `.default(false)` and a refinement sees the parsed value, so `{ modifyAllRecords: true }` parsed to `{ allowDelete: false, modifyAllRecords: true }` on `origin/main` 6021b5e (measured on the built dist). A refinement alone would refuse that output the next time it is parsed: `definePermissionSet` output handed to `defineStack`, a build re-read at boot, a stored row saved again. So the explicitness has to be read off the raw input. The stage writes `true` into an omitted key (which is what `objectPermissionGrants` already answers), and the refinement then only ever sees an authored `false`. `parse(parse(x))` equals `parse(x)` is pinned.

The same default is why data at rest carries the pair where nobody wrote it: the real HotCRM 17.1 built artifact fixture (`packages/metadata/src/__fixtures__/hotcrm-17.1-built-permissions.artifact.json`) has `sales_manager.crm_forecast` = `allowDelete: false` beside `modifyAllRecords: true`. Hence the D2 conversion. The artifact door now converts it (17.1 floor) and refuses the same body when it claims a surface past `retiredAfter`; both are pinned in `plugin-artifact-forward-conversion.test.ts`.

## Reading: can a criteria rule select every row, and does it grant edit without delete?

Read: `checkDelete` in `plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts` has no share branch (ADR-0111 D3), so an `edit` share opens update and never delete. `rule-criteria.ts` `isMatchAllCriteria` refuses or skips a criteria that lowers to an empty filter, and accepts any concrete field predicate.

Measured on a booted in-process stack (`@objectstack/verify` `bootStack`, at 9f2f3fa31, whose runtime code the later commits do not touch; a temporary test, not committed), the card's own `srm_material` shape: `public_read`, admin-owned rows, permission set `{ allowRead, allowCreate: false, allowEdit, allowDelete: false }` distributed by position `srm_buyer`, rule `{ type: 'criteria', condition: "record.id != ''", accessLevel: 'edit', sharedWith: { type: 'position', value: 'srm_buyer' } }`:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| buyer updates an admin-owned row, before holding the position | 403 PERMISSION_DENIED |
| `sys_user_position` row inserted | one `sys_record_share` row, `edit`, `source: rule`, to the buyer |
| buyer updates the admin-owned row | 200, `category` written, owner unchanged |
| buyer deletes it | 403 PERMISSION_DENIED; row still present |
| admin inserts a new row; buyer updates / deletes it | 200 / 403 |
| buyer creates a row | 403 |

Control, same stack with `condition: 'true'`: boot logs `declared rule not served … reason: match-all-criteria`, no share row, and the buyer holding the position is refused the same update at the record ("You do not have access to this record"). So the update above came from the share. A literal `true` is not refused at parse; it is never served. The docs and every prescription say so.

## Producers

Measured on 6021b5e before the change: no permission set in `examples/**`, `packages/platform-objects`, plugins or services authors the pair. Two producers set `modifyAllRecords: true` and omit `allowDelete`, and now parse to `allowDelete: true` with no edit: `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts` `showcase_ops.showcase_announcement` and `packages/verify/src/parent-write-reach.ts` `modifyAll`. The platform sets (`admin_full_access`, `organization_admin`) write `allowDelete: true` explicitly. Raw evaluator fixtures that declare the pair (`plugin-security` `security-plugin.test.ts` "should allow edit/delete via modifyAllRecords") are never parsed and keep pinning the runtime semantics the ruling keeps.

## Tests and gates

All readings at head `c5b702ced`.

- **Derived gates** (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`): 116 derived, 116 run, every exit captured before any pipe; `--ran` with exit codes answers "116 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)". One gate (`check-comment-mask-corpus`) first went red on ENOENT for a temporary bundle the concurrent dogfood run wrote into `examples/app-showcase`; re-run alone it is green (10121 files, 0 disagree). `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` needed its pinned fixture commit fetched in this shallow clone; green after.
- **Package suites** (lock VERDICT exit 0 each): spec `test` 719 files / 21788 tests, spec `test:repo` 79 / 1269, spec `typecheck`; lint `test` 161 / 7274 and `typecheck`; metadata `test` 64 / 906 and `typecheck`.
- **Consumers of the contract** (each green): metadata-core 19 / 800; runtime 441 / 7080 and `test:repo` 3 / 854; core 118 / 2757 and `test:repo` 6 / 82; verify 46 / 393; metadata-protocol 263 / 21475; rest 320 / 6406 and `test:repo` 5 / 280; plugin-security 222 / 4628; cli `--project unit` 328 / 4816 (integration layer declared to CI: the diff touches no CLI spawn entry).
- **Dogfood battery** (`(narrowing)` arm): 295 passed, 3 skipped files; 2520 passed, 18 skipped tests; VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `check:dev-prereqs`: green (local-only).
- No ablation: the refusal and the materialisation are pinned by tests whose subject is `src/` (spec's own suite), and the lint and artifact-door pins read rebuilt `dist/` (rebuilt before each run).

## Acceptance notes

- `GetObjectPermissionsResponseSchema.permissions` uses the authoring `ObjectPermissionSchema` (not the effective one), so it inherits the refusal, as it already inherits the #16870 scope refusals. Noted, not changed.
- `os migrate meta --from 17` replays the retired D2 entry, so a source carrying the pair would be rewritten to `allowDelete: true` (the runtime behaviour) with the D3 entry listed beside it as the judgment owed. Recorded in the D3 entry's `conversionIds`.
- The no-share control above also shows the platform's write floor on a `public_read` object: without the share, the update is refused at the record, not at the object CRUD check.
